questions.question: Which analysis population was used in the trial of app-based CBT-I versus app-based health education, and what were the new-onset MDD event counts and randomized denominators over 12 months, the primary Cox HR with its reported interval, and the additionally adjusted exploratory HR with its interval and added covariates?
questions.expected_answer_as_reported: Intent-to-treat: CBT-I 37/354 (10%) and HE 62/354 (18%) developed new-onset MDD during 12 months. Primary HR 0.58 (0.38–0.87). The exploratory additionally adjusted HR was 0.60 (0.40–0.90), after adding prior history of MDD, educational level, family income, comorbid medical illnesses, and use of sleep-promoting medications. The exploratory estimate is separate from the primary estimate.

provisional_spans.quote: Analyses were conducted based on the intent-to-treat approach.

Thirty-seven participants (incidence proportion, 10%; 37/354) in the intervention group and 62 participants (incidence proportion, 18%; 62/354) in the control group developed new-onset MDD during the 12-month follow-up.
Cox regression revealed an HR of 0.58 (0.38–0.87; p = 0.008) for MDD favoring app-based CBT-I intervention.

708 participants (407 females [57%]; mean age, 22.1 years [SD = 1.9]) were randomly allocated to app-based CBT-I group (n = 354) or app-based HE group (n = 354). Thirty-seven participants (10%) in the intervention group and 62 participants (18%) in the control group developed new-onset MDD throughout the 12-month follow-up, with a hazard ratio of 0.58 (95% confidence interval 0.38–0.87; p = 0.008).

After additionally adjusting for prior history of MDD, educational level, family income, comorbid medical illnesses, and use of sleep-promoting medications in exploratory analysis, the risk of developing MDD remained significantly lower for the app-based CBT-I intervention group compared with the controls (adjusted HR 0.60 [0.40–0.90]; p = 0.01)

questions.question: For the post-intervention insomnia-disorder outcome, which three criteria defined remission, and what weighted remission percentages and RR with 95% CI were reported for CBT-I versus health education after accounting for strata and missing-data patterns?
questions.expected_answer_as_reported: Remission required no functional impairments or distress with sleep; insomnia symptoms less than three times per week for at least 1 month; and sleep-promoting medication use less than once per week in the past month. The weighted post-intervention percentages were CBT-I 52% versus HE 28%, RR 1.83 (95% CI 1.49–2.24), after controlling for strata variables and accounting for missing-data patterns.

provisional_spans.quote: Remission of insomnia disorder was determined by the following criteria [21]: (1) no functional impairments or distress with sleep, (2) insomnia symptoms less than three times per week for at least 1 month, and (3) sleep-promoting medication use less than once per week in the past month.

At post-intervention, the weighted percentage of remitters based on clinical interviews in app-based CBT-I group was higher than that of the app-based HE group (52% versus 28%; relative risk [RR] 1.83 [95% CI 1.49–2.24]; p < 0.001) after controlling for strata variables and accounting for the missing data patterns.

Remission rates of insomnia were analyzed using a weighted generalized estimating equations model. Weights were computed as the product of a missing model weight to attenuate the effect of attrition conditional on strata variables and group allocation [32].

questions.question: In the subset with two health examinations, what mean interval (SD) between examinations and count and percentage progressing to a more severe CKM stage were reported, and why did the authors still caution about power despite similar time-dependent sensitivity-analysis results?
questions.expected_answer_as_reported: The mean interval was 2.5 years (SD 2.4); 40,320 participants (18.3%) progressed to a more severe CKM stage. The main baseline-measurement limitation must not be turned into a claim that no longitudinal sensitivity analysis occurred.
